title: Is quitting smoking contagious?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss why smoking is hard to quit and whether quitting is contagious. They cover how nicotine works on the cholinergic and dopamine pathways and endorphins, claims about additives and free-based nicotine in cigarettes, and why smokers cough in the morning. The main segment covers the Farmington Heart Study, which found that quitting by a spouse, co-worker, friend or sibling lowered a smoker's odds of continuing, with effects extending to friends of friends. The episode ends with a closing segment where Chuck describes noodling (catching catfish by hand) as ridiculous.

segments.title: Opening banter and smoking chat
segments.summary: Hosts joke about smoking and wanting to smoke at work, then turn to Chantix (varenicline) and the FAA ban on it for air traffic controllers and pilots due to reported psychiatric side effects, which are unproven.

segments.title: How nicotine works in the brain
segments.summary: Nicotine activates nicotinic receptors and the cholinergic pathways, affecting focus and calm, and is linked to memory and Alzheimer's concerns. It also triggers dopamine reward pathways and endorphin release, which varies by person.

segments.title: Cigarette additives, free-base nicotine and morning cough
segments.summary: Hosts cite cigarette ingredient counts and tar accumulation, claim cigarette makers add free-base nicotine to increase addictiveness, and explain that the morning cough is cilia being numbed by smoking, so the first cigarette of the day seems to relieve it. They also note that about half of lung cancer surgery patients resume smoking.

segments.title: Farmington Heart Study and quitting as a social behavior
segments.summary: The Farmington Heart Study followed about 12,000 residents of Farmington, Massachusetts over 32 years. Quitting by a spouse, close friend, co-worker or sibling was linked to lower odds of continuing to smoke, with effects reaching friends of friends. Smokers tend to form clusters that break up when someone quits.

segments.title: Closing and advice to quit with a buddy
segments.summary: Josh urges smokers to quit with a buddy or spouse, and jokes that the first third of a cigarette is where the effect is.

segments.title: Noodling debate
segments.summary: Chuck says he finds noodling, catching catfish by reaching into underwater mud holes, ridiculous, while Josh notes it is also called stumping. They reference Flash Gordon and point listeners to HowStuffWorks for more on noodling.
